editorial.headline: Car Repair Is Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 95311 covers the practical work of keeping cars, trailers and semitrailers roadworthy—nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today. That is the decisive local reality for KBLI 95311, even though the activity is nationally classified as open to PMA with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali’s block follows its permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA activities carrying Low or Medium-Low risk; at the Large scale, every scope in this activity falls within those risk categories. The block is recorded under the Bali risk-class status and tied to the moratorium in force from May 2026.

The activity itself is the broad working life of a vehicle repair shop. It encompasses mechanical and electrical repair, electronic injection-system work, routine servicing, bodywork, component repair, spraying and painting, and the repair of vehicle glass, windows and seating. It also includes diagnosing and repairing mechatronic systems; fitting, replacing or repairing inner and outer tyres; anti-rust treatment; and installing parts and accessories where that installation is not part of a manufacturing process. Cars are central, but trailers and semitrailers are expressly within the scope as well.

Nationally, the activity is available at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the code is not framed as a narrow specialist trade: it accommodates both routine maintenance and a substantial range of technical, structural and finishing work. Its national PMA position is equally clear. It is TERBUKA, and the stated ceiling permits 100% foreign ownership. There is no need to infer a lower national cap from the operational diversity of the workshop.

Bali changes the practical conclusion without changing the national classification. The province’s rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration, island-wide and permanently. For this activity, the Large-scale OSS risk assessment is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, bringing it within that block. So the accurate reading is not that foreign ownership is nationally restricted; it is that a nationally open, fully foreign-ownable activity cannot presently be registered as PMA in Bali.
